how_to_tell_apart: Finnish is typologically close to Estonian but the everyday words diverge quickly: minä/sinä, olen/en, mitä, että, kiitos, anteeksi, täällä and älä are Finnish, whereas Estonian uses ma/sa, olen/ei, mis, et, aitäh or tänan, and palun. Finnish also lacks the letter õ, which is a strong Estonian cue. Swedish may appear in the same country, but it is Germanic (jag, inte, och) and uses å, which Finnish native words do not.

uncertain: hei is frequent in Finnish greetings but also in Norwegian, so it is listed as shared and not treated as a Finnish-only cue.
Colloquial Finnish often shortens minä to mä and sinä to sä; those forms are common on the phone but were not counted separately from the standard pronouns.
